newsitem.title: USA: US Airways says to cut U.S.-Canada fares.
newsitem.headline: US Airways says to cut U.S.-Canada fares.

text.p: US Airways said on Tuesday that it had lowered ticket prices by as much as 55 percent for round-trip fares bought no later than August 21.
In a statement, the airline said the cuts applied to round-trip fares in nearly 8,000 U.S. and Canada markets, as well as flights to San Juan, Grand Cayman, Montego Bay and Cancun.
Under the fare sale, reservations must be made at least 14 days prior to departure and trips must include at least one Saturday night stay, US Airways said.
Delta Air Lines spokesman said the US Airways fare cuts were a response to Northwest Airlines Corp's fare cuts that were announced August 11.
The Delta spokesman said the carrier, which had adapted its fares to Northwest's cuts, will be competitive with US Airways fares.
American Airlines also matched the Northwest fare cuts, a company spokesman said.
Analysts did not expect the sale to greatly impact long-term fares.
"This sounds like normal seasonal discounting that happens every year," said Morgan Stanley analyst Kevin Murphy, adding, "It's probably part of their business plan."
